The ARN of the role that you specify can\u2019t include a path other than `/`. For example, if the name of your role is `development/apps/my-role`, you\u2019d need to change it to `my-role` when specifying the ARN for the role. Make sure that you specify the node IAM role ARN (not the instance profile ARN).\\\\n\\\\n If the nodes are self-managed, and you haven\u2019t created access entries for the ARN of the node\u2019s IAM role, then run the same commands listed for managed nodes. For **Type**, select\\xa0**EC2\\\\\\\\_linux**\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/eks-nodes-fail-cluster-join\"}]}}\\n\\n## Recent AWS announcements (What\\'s New)\\n\\nNewer than your training data may be. {"id": "b2aad300-03c6-42e4-95b5-53f7ae0e6b64", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Found it — that confirms the root cause. Here's the issue:

**The role ARN with a path breaks aws-auth matching.**

Your role ARN is `[redacted ARN]` — note the path `/teams/platform/` between `role/` and the role name. AWS documentation is explicit on this:

> *"The ARN of the role that you specify can't include a path other than `/`. For example, if the name of your role is `development/apps/my-role`, you'd need to change it to `my-role` when specifying the ARN for the role."*

So even though you added the "exact" ARN to `mapRoles`, EKS's authenticator (aws-iam-authenticator) strips/ignores the path when matching the role, and matches only against the role name component. Pasting the full path-qualified ARN into `rolearn` is a well-known trap — it looks correct, but the authenticator's internal matching logic doesn't handle custom paths the way you'd expect, so the mapping effectively doesn't match and the node's STS identity comes back as unauthorized.

**How to fix it:**
1. In the `mapRoles` entry, use the ARN *without* the path — i.e. `[redacted ARN]` (even though the role's actual path is `/teams/platform/`, specify it as if it had no path).
2. Also double check:
   - You're using the **node IAM role ARN**, not the instance profile ARN (a different common mix-up).
   - `username` is set to `system:node:{{EC2PrivateDNSName}}` and `groups` includes `system:bootstrappers` and `system:nodes`.
   - If this cluster uses EKS access entries instead of (or alongside) aws-auth, the path restriction doesn't apply the same way, but you'd want to create an access entry for the full-path role ARN instead.

Want me to check whether this cluster is using access entries vs. the aws-auth ConfigMap, or pull the current `aws-auth` ConfigMap content to confirm the exact mismatch? I'd just need the cluster name/account/region.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
